name: Cagrilintide

lead: Cagrilintide is a long-acting analogue of amylin, a hormone that signals fullness. People use or follow it as an appetite suppressant for getting lean, alone or alongside semaglutide.

It acts on amylin and calcitonin receptors in the brain, reducing appetite and food intake and slowing stomach emptying. In the REDEFINE 1 study, cagrilintide alone produced a mean body-weight reduction of 11.8 percent versus 2.3 percent for placebo after 68 weeks. A fixed combination with semaglutide, CagriSema, has phase 3 results published in 2025.

paras: In trials it is a once-weekly injection. Because its pathway differs from GLP-1, it is paired with semaglutide for additive effect. Outside trials, research-labelled supplies appear on the grey market.

Trial reports describe mainly gastrointestinal effects such as nausea and vomiting, which are dose-related. Long-term safety is still being assessed and it is not approved as a standalone product. Unregulated research-chemical supplies are of unverified quality.

forums.title: Cagrilintide- The hidden secret to complete appetite suppression

angle.text: Cagrilintide is an experimental amylin analogue used alone or with semaglutide to suppress appetite and cut body fat. It works by boosting fullness signals so you eat less and carry less fat; fat loss is studied in trial populations, while looks-focused "leanmaxxing" use is discussed by users.

lead: Cagrilintide is a long-acting analogue of amylin, a pancreatic hormone released with insulin after meals that signals fullness. Developed by Novo Nordisk and injected once weekly in trials, it is studied for obesity and type 2 diabetes, alone and in a fixed combination with semaglutide called CagriSema [1][2][3]. The appearance link runs through body composition: reduced appetite leads to lower calorie intake, which leads to fat loss, which leads to a leaner face and physique. This is the route that 'leanmaxxing' threads on looksmax.org describe when they discuss it [4].

In a 2021 phase 2 dose-finding trial of 706 adults with overweight or obesity, 26 weeks of cagrilintide produced average weight losses of 6.0 to 10.8 percent across dose groups, against 3.0 percent with placebo and 9.0 percent with liraglutide at its highest comparison dose [5]. In the 68-week REDEFINE 1 phase 3 trial, published in 2025, the combination with semaglutide produced a mean 20.4 percent weight reduction against 3.0 percent with placebo [6]. Per Wikipedia's summary of the trial data, the cagrilintide-only arm lost 11.5 percent on one analysis and 11.8 percent on another that accounted for adherence [3][1].

Cagrilintide has no approved indication as a stand-alone product. Its evidence base consists largely of company-sponsored trial publications, pharmacology papers and reviews. No published trial has measured facial appearance as an outcome, although a registered phase 1 study is examining how cagrilintide-containing treatments affect muscle health during weight loss [7].

paras: Cagrilintide is a lipidated peptide analogue of human amylin, built to last about a week in the body so that it can be injected once weekly rather than several times a day [2][8]. It is also catalogued as AM833 in early pharmacology work and under the code GLXC-26801 on Wikipedia [9][1]. Novo Nordisk is the developer, and the program is part of a wider effort to add amylin-pathway drugs to the GLP-1 drugs that have dominated obesity medicine [10][11].

It is distinct from the semaglutide and tirzepatide products that are approved for weight management. Where those act on incretin receptors, cagrilintide acts on amylin and calcitonin receptors, which is why researchers describe the combination in CagriSema as using two complementary appetite pathways [10][6].

sections.h: How people use it to improve their looks
paras: The route to a better appearance is indirect and runs through body fat. Appetite suppression reduces calorie intake, and sustained fat loss thins the face, sharpens jaw and cheek definition and reveals muscle. Looksmaxxing communities call this 'leanmaxxing', and a looksmax.org thread describes it as the most effective single improvement and presents pharmaceutical appetite suppressants as a way to make it easier [4].

The same thread describes cagrilintide as an underrated option, citing the roughly 11.8 percent weight reduction reported for the drug alone and explaining the biology of amylin signalling to its readers [4]. Cagrilintide has no known action on facial fat specifically; its effect is on appetite and body weight as a whole.

Lean mass is a related concern in physique-focused circles because weight lost on appetite-suppressing drugs can include muscle as well as fat. A phase 1 study registered in 2026 aims to examine the effect of CagriSema, cagrilintide and semaglutide on muscle health, and the sponsor titles it as investigating the role of amylin signalling in muscle [7].

Amylin is a 37-amino-acid hormone secreted by pancreatic beta cells together with insulin in a ratio of roughly one part to one hundred. It slows gastric emptying, reduces glucagon and promotes fullness, acting largely through the area postrema in the brainstem [12]. Researchers characterised it in 1987 after earlier work on amyloid deposits in the islets of people with diabetes [12]. Natural amylin readily aggregates into amyloid fibrils, which complicates its use as a drug [2].

Cagrilintide activates amylin receptors, which are complexes of the calcitonin receptor with receptor activity-modifying proteins, and also calcitonin receptors. A 2021 pharmacology paper compared it with pramlintide, salmon calcitonin and other agonists across 25 endpoints and found a distinct profile of binding, activation and receptor regulation [9]. A 2025 mouse study reported that cagrilintide reduced food intake and body weight and that its effect depended on amylin receptors 1 and 3: mice lacking the supporting proteins showed a 57 percent lower activation signal in the area postrema [13].

Forum authors summarise the mechanism as mimicking amylin, activating calcitonin and RAMP receptors in the brainstem and slowing gastric emptying [4]. Reviews of amylin biology describe the same pathway [14].

Pramlintide, an earlier amylin analogue made by Amylin Pharmaceuticals, was approved by the FDA on 16 March 2005 for adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who use mealtime insulin [15]. Its short half-life requires multiple daily injections. Cagrilintide's design, described in a 2021 Journal of Medicinal Chemistry paper, was aimed at keeping the stability and satiety effects while extending duration [2].

A phase 1b trial of 95 participants tested cagrilintide with semaglutide 2.4 mg for weight management. At week 20 the mean weight reduction was 17.1 percent in one cagrilintide arm and 15.7 percent in another, against 9.8 percent with pooled placebo. Cagrilintide's half-life measured 159 to 195 hours, and the authors described the combination as well tolerated, with gastrointestinal events making up 37 percent of 566 adverse events [8].

The 2021 phase 2 trial in The Lancet randomised 706 adults in ten countries to several cagrilintide doses, liraglutide 3.0 mg or placebo for 26 weeks. Cagrilintide groups lost 6.0 to 10.8 percent of body weight versus 3.0 percent for placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events occurred in 41 to 63 percent of cagrilintide recipients and 32 percent of the placebo group, nausea in 20 to 47 percent versus 18 percent, and about 10 percent of participants permanently stopped treatment [5].

A 32-week phase 2 trial of 92 adults with type 2 diabetes at 17 US sites reported weight losses of 15.6 percent with CagriSema, 5.1 percent with semaglutide and 8.1 percent with cagrilintide. Reductions in HbA1c were greater with CagriSema than with cagrilintide but not significantly different from semaglutide [16].

REDEFINE 1, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2025, randomised 3,417 adults without diabetes who had obesity or overweight with a complication. Over 68 weeks the mean weight change was -20.4 percent with CagriSema and -3.0 percent with placebo. Gastrointestinal events were reported by 79.6 percent of the combination group and 39.9 percent of placebo recipients, mostly transient and mild to moderate [6]. Wikipedia lists the single-agent arms in this trial as 11.5 percent for cagrilintide and 14.9 percent for semaglutide on one analysis [3].

REDEFINE 2 enrolled 1,206 adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes. Mean weight change was -13.7 percent with CagriSema versus -3.4 percent with placebo at 68 weeks, and 73.5 percent of the combination group reached an HbA1c of 6.5 percent or lower versus 15.9 percent on placebo [17]. A later trial, REDEFINE 5, is described by Wikipedia as comparing CagriSema with semaglutide in 331 participants, with estimated changes of -18.4 and -11.7 percent respectively [3].

Phase 3 registrations for cagrilintide itself include two weight-management trials with 300 and 330 participants, the latter in people with type 2 diabetes, both listed as started in November 2025, and a further trial comparing two versions of the injectable [18][19][20]. A phase 1 study registered in 2026 examines tolerability in people who stopped GLP-1 drugs because of gastrointestinal effects [21]. A 2023 phase 1 study examined effects on heart rhythm in healthy volunteers [22].

A 2024 meta-analysis pooled three randomised trials with 430 participants. CagriSema produced about 9 percentage points more weight loss than semaglutide 2.4 mg at 20 to 32 weeks, while cagrilintide alone produced weight loss similar to semaglutide or liraglutide and was associated with significantly less vomiting [23].

Across trials the most frequent adverse events are gastrointestinal, mainly nausea and vomiting, and they are dose-related and usually mild to moderate [5][6][17]. Reviews of next-generation obesity drugs describe long-term safety as still being assessed [11][10]. The quality and content of cagrilintide products sold outside clinical trials has not been assessed in the published literature.

Eli Lilly's eloralintide is another amylin receptor agonist in clinical development for obesity [24]. Reviews of the pipeline describe amylin analogues as one of several mechanisms, alongside GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptor drugs, being combined to increase weight loss [11][10][25].

Cagrilintide appears in looksmaxxing discussion as part of 'leanmaxxing', fat loss pursued for facial and physique definition. The single thread documented here sets out the biology, quotes the trial weight-loss figure and frames cagrilintide as an addition to existing fat-loss approaches [4].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, cagrilintide is presented as an underrated appetite suppressant for 'leanmaxxing' [4].

claims.claim: Cagrilintide alone gives strong appetite suppression and weight loss.
It works by mimicking amylin in the brainstem and slowing gastric emptying.
Leanmaxxing with pharmaceuticals is the most effective way to improve looks.

timeline.event: Amylin is characterised after earlier observations of islet amyloid in diabetes [12].
Pramlintide, the first amylin analogue, is approved by the FDA [15].
Development of cagrilintide is described in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry and its pharmacology is published [2][9].
Phase 2 dose-finding trial in 706 adults and phase 1b combination trial with semaglutide are published [5][8].
Phase 2 trial of CagriSema in type 2 diabetes, 92 participants, is published in The Lancet [16]; CagriSema enters phase 3 [3].
Meta-analysis of three randomised trials of cagrilintide and CagriSema is published [23].
REDEFINE 1 and REDEFINE 2 are published in the New England Journal of Medicine [6][17].
Phase 3 trials of cagrilintide alone begin [18][19].
Phase 1 studies on muscle health and on GLP-1 intolerance are registered [7][21].
